newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks rise slightly in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks rise slightly in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged up in early trading on Friday after opening weaker due to profit-taking and caution ahead of U.S. inflation reports due out later, brokers said.
"The market is likely to go softer throughout the day, said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was trading up 13 points at 12,255.81 on active turnover of HK$1.7 billion, off a low of 12,201.12.
"The near term trend in the market will depend on U.S. economic figures," said Li. On Friday, the U.S. government will report the September producer price index as well as September retail sales.
Friday's data are expected to give financial markets an indication of whether the U.S. Federal Reserve will soon have to hike interest rates in order to cool inflation.
Technical analysts were negative on the near-term trend but remained bullish on the longer term outlook.
"The index has already reached my monthly target of 12,228," said Ted Chen, technical analyst at Technical Data Inc.
"It is looking highly overbought. I am forecasting a near-term correction to the 12,000-12,050 level, followed by the establishment of a trading range based above 12,000, said Chen.
The Hang Seng Index has advanced more than 1,000 points since September 12.
Properties rebounded to lead the market in early trade, followed by the commercial and industrial sector. rotational buying also boosted mid-sized issues.

Hopewell led the property sector with a gain of HK$0.57 to HK$5.05. The company announced on Thursday Southern Co would take an 80 percent in subsidiary Consolidated Electric Power Asia (CEPA) in a move which analysts said will reduce Hopewell's cash flow and earnings as well as debt burden.
Sun Hung Kai Properties bounded to a new high of HK$87.25 in early trade then eased to HK$87.00, a gain of HK$0.50.
Swire Pacific was unchanged at HK$70.50, while CITIC Pacific was rose HK$0.30 to HK$36.50 and Cathay Pacific put on HK$0.15 to HK$12.85.

In the mid-cap sector, Winsor Industrial gained HK$0.40 to HK$7.15 on the release of details of the spin-off of the company's property assets into a separate listing. HKR International gained HK$0.30 to HK9.60.
